reason: Conversation 1 picks up the new drawer unit as the key clue and diagnoses overheat protection from restricted ventilation. It gives safe, non-invasive checks (a torch look, emptying the top drawer, easing off boost) and tells the customer to take the installer's clearance instructions back to the fitter. It also keeps the fan, sensor and board as a fallback needing an engineer, without claiming a faulty part. Conversation 2 asks irrelevant questions (isolator, breaker, burning smell), never uses the drawer clue, and ends with a generic engineer referral plus an electrical-trip safety panel that doesn't fit the facts, so it gives no useful diagnosis or ventilation advice.
